quick.summary: Why polite users hide the truth, and how to spot real problems.
quick.takeaway: Do not just ask what they think. Give them a goal and watch silently.

beats.line: Users said the payment flow was clear. Why did everyone abandon it?
Think of a restaurant. Diners say they love the new healthy menu.
But then they order a giant fried burger anyway.
Right. People just want to look good to you.
Exactly. When testing, you cannot just ask if they like the design.
This gap is called social desirability bias.
Can I just say people tell white lies?
Yes. Watch what they do, do not just listen.
So I should give them a goal and just watch their clicks silently.
That is how you find the real problem.

quiz.question: You are testing a new checkout page. What is the most reliable signal of success?
options: Users rate it highly on a survey.
Users say they prefer it to the old one.
Users successfully buy an item without asking for help.
Users comment on the nice colors.
quiz.explanation: Actions speak louder than opinions. Watching them complete the task proves the design works.

quiz.question: A user's opinion is the only thing that matters in usability testing.
quiz.explanation: Users often say what they think you want to hear. Their behavior reveals the truth.
